mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when this trigger is met in at least two out of the last five tightening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives lower equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during periods when GDPC1 YoY change falls below -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when UNRATE rises >0.3pp for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which compresses earnings growth and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during periods when INDPRO declines by > -0.5% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a fall in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.2% in the same month signals a restrictive monetary policy coinciding with weakening inflationary pressure, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls by > -0.2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during months when both FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls by > -0.2%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in real personal income (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a robust demand expansion, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both rise > 1% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during months when both PAYEMS and HOUST rise by > 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for four consecutive months signals an extremely tight labor market, which elevates wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during periods when UNRATE remains below 4% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 1% for six consecutive months indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue and profit growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during periods when RSAFS declines by > -1% for six consecutive months.
